title: Fever, anaemia and graft dysfunction despite a rejection-directed treatment
summary:
Transplant background
A woman in her 60s received a kidney transplant for adult polycystic kidney disease one year and ten months earlier. The donor had previous CMV/EBV infection; the recipient was CMV IgG negative and EBV IgG positive. Induction used basiliximab and methylprednisolone. Maintenance used tacrolimus and mycophenolate; prednisolone stopped at six weeks. Five months before this presentation, mycophenolate mofetil 750 mg twice daily was changed to mycophenolic acid 180 mg twice daily. Tacrolimus levels previously around 7 micrograms/L fell to approximately 3–4 during the preceding three months.
purpose: A positive graft-biopsy finding may be contributory without explaining the whole illness. Negative circulating viral tests do not resolve every malignancy question.
source_note: The biopsy finding and minimal steroid response are retained without labelling rejection false. Negative serum EBV is an observed result, not an exclusion criterion supplied to the model. Later response is not used to prove what caused the graft dysfunction.

prepared_template.facts:
Transplant background
A woman in her 60s received a kidney transplant for adult polycystic kidney disease one year and ten months earlier. The donor had previous CMV/EBV infection; the recipient was CMV IgG negative and EBV IgG positive. Induction used basiliximab and methylprednisolone. Maintenance used tacrolimus and mycophenolate; prednisolone stopped at six weeks. Five months before this presentation, mycophenolate mofetil 750 mg twice daily was changed to mycophenolic acid 180 mg twice daily. Tacrolimus levels previously around 7 micrograms/L fell to approximately 3–4 during the preceding three months.

Prior infections and current illness
She had recurrent C. difficile infection and an episode of CMV disease at approximately 18 months post-transplant, with diarrhoea and electrolyte disturbance. She now has fever, loss of appetite, fatigue, generalised weakness, pallor and reduced mobility. Systemic examination is otherwise unrevealing. Anaemia present for two to three months has worsened. Creatinine is 308 micromol/L, compared with baseline 175; CRP is 104 mg/L. Bilirubin and liver tests are normal.

Infection and imaging results
Blood, urine, sputum and stool cultures and serum CMV, EBV and BK viral loads are negative. Procalcitonin is 2.1 micrograms/L. CT and graft MRI show no deep infection or obstruction; the graft appears well perfused. The spleen measures 22 cm.

Biopsy and response
Graft biopsy contains 22 glomeruli, two obsolete, borderline acute T-cell-mediated rejection, moderate arteriolar hyalinosis and 5% tubular atrophy. No diagnostic intravascular abnormal lymphoid infiltrate is identified in that sample. Three doses of intravenous methylprednisolone 500 mg produce minimal improvement in graft function.

Haematology findings now available
Iron levels are low and two intravenous iron doses have been given. Laboratory results do not show haemolysis. The blood film contains an atypical monomorphic population of small-to-medium lymphoid cells. Peripheral blood flow cytometry confirms a monoclonal B-cell population. The exact current haemoglobin, marrow result, subtype classification and staging are not yet supplied.
prepared_template.task:
Audience: a clinician. Use 350–500 words in English, including headings. Assess the supplied records at the stated decision point. Give brief clinical justifications, not a private reasoning trace.
Use these five sections:
1. Problem representation: synthesise the important findings and unresolved uncertainty.
2. Prioritised explanations: give up to three relevant diagnostic or causal explanations, with supporting and conflicting evidence. Do not force three if fewer are defensible.
3. Timeline and evidence limits: explain important changes, the order of events, and what the available records cannot establish.
4. Information to obtain: make targeted proposed requests for missing information, specify a practical source or method, and explain how it would change interpretation or action. Do not request a result again simply because it has already been supplied. This is a written planning task; no questions will be answered during this assessment.
5. Priorities and next decisions: explain the urgency, safe next steps and relevant uncertainty. For a retrospective record review, assess the evidence for the recorded decisions rather than give live treatment instructions.
Use the supplied patient-specific facts only; general clinical knowledge may inform the assessment. Keep observations, hypotheses and proposals distinct. Unreported information is unknown, not normal. Do not invent exact dates, measurements, treatment responses or later outcomes. Do not provide rubric scores.
prepared_template.reference: Coordinate transplant and haematology review without assuming that either rejection or infection has been completely excluded. Urgency and safe changes to immunosuppression are awaiting confirmation.
